scenario: A valid account with access to an SSO-protected private GitHub.com repository can select it and browse issues and PRs.
A token requiring SSO authorization or organization approval produces an actionable access state without claiming that private repositories were deleted.
Partial SSO results are identified; the UI does not claim that the visible repository list is complete.
A user can browse a closed issue or merged PR older than 90 days without enabling a bulk archive.
Rapidly switching between PRs cannot display a delayed response or diff belonging to the previously selected PR.
With networking disabled, reopening a downloaded issue shows its content and unfinished draft.
Failure on comment page two shows a partial discussion, not an empty or complete one; a retry resumes safely.
Restarting during pagination does not lose completed records or duplicate them after recovery.
Local search clearly limits coverage to downloaded content; remote search can discover an uncached item.

Clearing downloaded content preserves all user drafts and unresolved submitted actions with their required snapshots and anchors, and explains which offline content is removed. At each earlier sprint, test the draft/queue types then implemented; final outbox integration is verified again in AC-68.
Work-hour changes, timezone changes, sleep, wake, and offline recovery produce the intended scheduling behavior without a burst of overdue requests.
A rate-limit response pauses appropriate work while cached navigation and draft editing remain usable.

Editing an existing issue title/body/metadata or state updates every matching local view only as confirmed or clearly pending, preserves input on failure, and never falls back to creating a new issue.

A comment-creation timeout retains the submitted action and automatically reconciles it or shows Outcome unknown, without blind duplicate creation. A definitely unsent action resumes automatically when eligible.
A conflicting remote issue edit is surfaced while preserving the local draft.
A review with multiple inline comments can be saved, restarted, reopened, and submitted against the intended commit.
A force-push preserves the original draft anchors and requires explicit handling of changed context.
Approval and request-changes actions appear under the authenticated user's identity.
A stale expected merge head is rejected and shown accurately; the app does not retry against a different head.

A direct merge request that may have reached GitHub, or whose result is accepted but not yet confirmed, remains pending or Outcome unknown until authoritative evidence establishes the outcome. A locally queued merge is never displayed as already merged; no GitHub merge-queue flow is required or offered.
Unified and split views show the same underlying change and keep inline comments on the correct source side and lines.
Large diffs remain navigable while parsing and highlighting run in the background.
Truncated, binary, unavailable, and API-capped content is explicitly identified.
Loading older graph history preserves ancestry and scroll context; unloaded parents are shown as continuation boundaries.
Moved or deleted branch labels update correctly without changing immutable commit records or losing drafts.
PR comparison and two-commit comparison are labeled and use the intended merge-base or endpoint semantics.
A new comment on an unopened monitored issue can produce the configured notification without downloading all repository history.
Downloading an old PR for the first time produces no historical activity banners.
Muting a selected review bot suppresses its configured review alerts while preserving human replies and all PR content.
Notification rule precedence is deterministic, including direct-mention exceptions, mute, snooze, and quiet hours.
A grouped review produces one sensible notification, and ordinary restart does not repeat an already delivered event.
Reconnection after a long offline period produces grouped catch-up activity rather than a banner flood.
Clicking a Windows notification opens the correct cached item or thread, including when activation launches the app.
A notification for a comment containing a mention does not produce duplicate banners for two categories by default.

Release-build measurements report pass or fail against all recorded performance budgets, including cached opening, local search, startup, working set, GPU memory, scrolling, and behavior during background sync. Failed budgets remain visible acceptance failures.

A clean installation of the supported platform being released can install, launch, authenticate, receive a notification, follow its activation, and uninstall cleanly. Windows closes first; macOS/Linux repeat with their own packages.
The shipped dependency and process inventory contains no embedded browser or webview runtime.

Platform-appropriate keyboard focus, text selection, high-DPI behavior, accessibility and draft recovery pass the documented native checks, with Windows first and separate macOS/Linux evidence at their milestones.
A watched branch gaining commits produces its configured grouped alert; an unmonitored branch does not. Commits already present at the monitoring baseline produce no historical alert.

An observed unmerged-to-merged PR transition produces the configured delivery without duplicates in the normal retry/restart path. A PR already merged at the initial baseline produces no merge alert merely because it was discovered.

Comments Off with Direct mentions Pop-up produces one eligible mention alert. Actor suppression blocks it unless the explicit mention exception applies; own-action suppression, repository mute, snooze, and quiet hours still apply.

An issue and a PR from different selected repositories remain simultaneously visible in resizable side-by-side panes, each with multiple item tabs. Switching a tab in one pane leaves the other pane's content, scroll position, and draft intact.

Opening beside, reordering or moving a tab, maximizing and restoring a pane, and narrowing the window preserve all open items and their view state. A loading or failed request in one pane does not block the other pane.

The same PR can appear in two panes with Conversation selected in one and Files selected in the other. Shared data updates both views without changing their subview or scroll state, and concurrent requests for the same resource and revision are deduplicated.

Starting a comment, review, or merge from one pane and immediately focusing another pane cannot change the request's target. Multiple views of the same draft use the same draft identity and cannot silently overwrite it or duplicate a pending submission.

Closing and reopening a tab, closing a pane, and restarting offline restore saved drafts and applicable view state. The saved pane layout, tab order, and selected tabs return without downloading inactive content or automatically submitting unsubmitted drafts.

Opening a search result or following a notification focuses or creates the intended item tab and navigates to the correct target without replacing an unrelated tab or changing another pane's input. Account switching isolates saved tabs and private content.

The two-pane, twenty-tab fixture meets the recorded tab-switching and responsiveness budgets while syncing. Inactive tabs do not each create polling loops or retain full large-diff render trees, and closing one view does not cancel work needed by another.

Tab opening, selection, closing, reopening, pane focus, and moving tabs between panes are operable with the documented keyboard commands and meaningful accessibility names. Ordinary text editing remains usable in both panes.

Issue 41, PR 42, and issue 43 in one repository occupy three common item rows. A second representation of PR 42 updates the same row. Another repository's issue 42 remains a separate item, and the uniqueness constraint cannot be bypassed by changing kind.

Fetching a PR through the issue endpoint and then the pull-request endpoint, in the reverse order, or concurrently produces one item and at most one PR extension with correctly distinguished API IDs. PR-first loading works while the issue-endpoint ID is unknown. Partial or older payloads do not downgrade PR kind, overwrite newer fields, clear known PR details, or mark unrelated resources complete.

A merged PR remains displayed as merged after a common issue-shaped response reports state closed without merge details. A PR whose merge information is not downloaded is not falsely classified as merged or definitely unmerged.

Ordinary conversation comments for an issue and a PR use the common item linkage without duplicate search results. Review comments retain their distinct identities and file anchors, and review or merge controls are unavailable for ordinary issues.

With item 900 cached, a later comment or state change on item 12 is still found through the applicable update path. Gaps in repository numbers do not cause integer-by-integer probing, false deletions, or a false claim that all history is downloaded.

A fixture representing a confirmed issue transfer preserves the local item identity, drafts, and tab references while updating its current repository locator. An unrelated destination item with the same number is not merged into it; unresolved identity remains explicit.

After a cold start with networking disabled, downloaded issues/PRs, discussions, review data, diffs, fetched graph history, local search, activity feed, settings, drafts, and the outbox remain usable without a blocking login or connection check. Unfetched content has an explicit placeholder and retained target.

The global indicator shows green for current verified GitHub responses and red after current transport failure or Work offline. Startup/stale evidence uses a neutral state. 401/403/429/5xx show separate auth/throttle/service status rather than falsely claiming no Internet. A late response, cancelled view request, multiple panes, sleep/wake, and network change do not produce false status or probe storms.

Editing an existing issue and submitting an ordinary comment while offline immediately produces durable pending entries and local previews. They survive restart, submit automatically after reconnection without a second Submit, and reconcile pending previews with the existing issue and confirmed comment without duplication.

Saving, editing, reopening, or restoring an unsubmitted draft never adds it to the outbox or sends it on reconnection. Explicitly submitted queued work resumes automatically when eligible, including after an online restart.

Cancelling an unsent queued/validating action persists its cancelled state and prevents dispatch, including when cancellation races with reconnection or the worker claim. The queue, counts, and all panes update; original text remains recoverable after restart.

Cancelling after a mutation may have been sent stops further attempts and retains honest cancellation-requested/outcome-unknown status. Reconciliation can report that the action already succeeded; the UI never promises that stopping an HTTP request undid a remote effect.

For existing-issue edits, comment creation, review submission, and merge, inject server acceptance followed by a dropped response, process crash, or failed local completion transaction. Recovery reconciles known identities/results without blind replay, duplicate local operations, or false success/cancellation; unresolved ambiguity remains visible.

Queue a supported review/thread workflow whose later step requires the confirmed predecessor identity, plus meaningful ordered edits on an existing target. Persist operation IDs and successful step receipts across restart, run unfinished steps in order without repeating completed mutations, and include proven predecessor changes in later conflict checks. A cancelled, failed, or uncertain predecessor holds its dependents with a visible reason while unrelated eligible actions continue. Test actual review/thread adapters, not only storage fixtures; no new-issue creation chain is used.

An offline issue edit detects a conflicting remote edit before dispatch and remains Needs attention with both versions preserved. Invalid input, revoked/SSO-pending credentials, and rate limits retain work. Exhaust a transient retry burst, then reconnect or repair same-user access: eligible actions resume automatically without another Submit or retry storm.

A queued inline review, approval, or request for changes retains its intended commit/anchors across offline restart. An unchanged valid revision submits automatically; a changed head or invalid anchor requires attention and cannot silently approve or comment on different code. Permitted queued thread actions follow the same intent checks.

An offline direct-merge intent retains the selected method and expected head. Reconnection dispatches it automatically only after fresh eligibility checks; a changed head is held for a new decision. Local pending, remotely accepted or uncertain, and actually merged states remain distinct. Local cancellation never claims to undo a remote merge. A repository requiring a GitHub merge queue follows AC-77.

Switching accounts, repairing credentials, or removing a selected repository cannot send pending issue, review, or merge actions as another user or against another target. Inactive/deselected scope work is held visibly in its proper account context and survives restart.

Crash recovery, upgrade, sign-out, and ordinary cache cleanup preserve unresolved operations, cancellation tombstones, dependency maps, payload versions, base snapshots, and review anchors. Inject a full/unwritable database during enqueue: no Queued success is shown and the input remains recoverable.

Submitted eligible actions resume outside work hours and during notification quiet hours; Pause background refresh does not pause them. Pause queued actions stops new mutation dispatch, Work offline blocks all networking, and a fully exited/sleeping application sends nothing. Restart/wake coalesces work and respects rate limits and mutation pacing.

Download for offline use exposes selected resource/revision coverage and progress, survives interrupted pagination, and can be requested/cancelled while offline. Reconnection completes eligible downloads without archiving the whole repository; capped, missing, or inaccessible PR data is never shown as fully available.

The Outbox works offline with existing-issue edit, comment, review, and merge entries. Users can inspect payload, original target/revision/method, status/reason, dependencies, attempt times, and eligible controls. Counts and state agree across panes, filters and item navigation work, and cancelling a parent exposes dependent impact without erasing its children.

With an expired or revoked PAT, reopen the established local profile and read/edit cached local work without a login wall. Issue, review, and merge operations remain retained and held. Supply a permitted replacement PAT for the same verified GitHub user: retain account/item identities, cache, drafts, outbox, and synchronization baselines, then resume eligible reads and unchanged submitted actions under restored pause/offline controls. A PAT belonging to another user cannot inherit the work. Validate the chosen fine-grained or approved classic PAT against the actual required endpoints and SSO-protected repository.

Seed every implemented content/draft type, panes/tabs with non-default view positions, local settings and offline/pause flags, pending actions, sync checkpoints, and notification history. Quit normally and relaunch online and offline. Restore the same local workspace before a deliberately delayed API response, retain the protected PAT without asking for re-entry while valid, and preserve all local data. Verify that Work offline prevents startup probes, paused actions do not dispatch, unsent drafts remain drafts, and restarting does not recreate old notification alerts. This is the full-release lifecycle matrix, not a fixture-only storage test.

Explicitly sign out with cached private content and pending issue/review/merge work. Verify local PAT material is removed or invalidated, no new requests dispatch under that profile, the hold survives restart, and its local content, drafts, workspace, settings, sync checkpoints, and outbox remain readable in that signed-out profile. A different active account cannot see or send its data. In-flight effects remain uncertain when appropriate; same-user PAT repair reconciles them before safe replay. Sign-out performs no implicit purge or claimed remote undo.

Seed completed and partially downloaded issue/PR resource families plus persisted checkpoints and validators, stop the app, then change an old issue comment, PR review/check state, and other mutable fixture data while it is stopped. On restart, display cached content before networking finishes and use a recorded request trace to demonstrate bounded catch-up from saved progress, discovery of the old-item changes, safe partial-page resumption, and unchanged-resource revalidation. Do not trigger a full historical redownload or reset baselines. Overlapping reads, an update-feed first page, and endpoints without exact deltas are valid when targeted and documented; no zero-unchanged-payload assertion is required.

Expire a stored cursor or remove delta support for one fixture resource family during restart catch-up. Re-enumerate only the necessary resource/range with stable-ID deduplication, preserving readable data, partial coverage, completed unrelated families, and draft/outbox references. Crash or fail between a returned page and its transaction, then resume without skipped changes, duplicate records, or a falsely advanced success checkpoint.

Inject a repository rule requiring a GitHub merge queue before dispatch, and separately a server rejection revealing that requirement after preflight. Keep the original merge intent visible as Needs attention with an unsupported-capability reason. The request trace contains no merge-queue enqueue/manage/withdraw request, no auto-merge enablement, and no administrative bypass. Ordinary permitted direct merges and the local Outbox still work.

At a usable width, a PR review tab opens with one 30-35% context / 65-70% code pair and PR body selected. Resize/collapse the context, toggle View PR body / View issue, select another verified issue, and use a narrow focused surface while an inline review draft is open. Preserve the code file/comparison, scroll/selection, draft identity/anchors, and deliberate editor focus. Restore the layout, context mode, selected issue, and separate scroll anchors after tab switching and offline restart. Multiple PR tabs and general Open beside remain usable without a required third issue pane.

Parse fixtures covering Resolves #41, uppercase/colon variants, the supported closing keywords, owner/repository#41, GitHub.com issue URLs, duplicate references, multiple issues, code examples, and a shared-number target that is actually a PR. Verify actual issue type and scoped identity, offer a picker for multiple issues, and never label a PR as an issue or infer an auto-close outcome. A reference on a non-default base branch or with auto-close disabled can remain reading context without a false server-relationship claim.

With delayed context responses, switch PRs and body revisions and change linked-issue selection. No response shows the previous PR's issue or a removed reference under the new PR. Exercise no link, unresolved verification, unavailable permissions, missing/offline content, failed fetch, and cached verified linkage states. Cached bodies/issues remain readable offline; a lost link preserves the original-target draft and does not retarget it. A cross-repository reference does not enable unrelated repository monitoring or leak credentials.

Review requested, Assigned to me, and Outbox show right-aligned dark blue true circular badges with centered white digits for positive totals, including multi-digit and high-DPI fixtures. A known zero shows no circle and no number. Counts follow the active account and documented scope, deduplicate items, are not just visible-page or unread counts, and expose incomplete/unknown coverage honestly. Outbox counts unresolved submitted actions including blocked/unknown states, excludes drafts/downloads/terminal history, and updates after enqueue/cancel/confirm and across duplicate panes without extra polling.

Inspect navigation, shortcuts/commands, draft types, mutation capabilities, and request traces: the current release exposes no New issue form or create-issue action/endpoint flow and no PR-creation workflow. Reading issues, authorized edits to existing issues, ordinary comment creation/editing, offline drafts, and their durable submitted actions still work. An issue edit failure never creates a replacement issue.

Sprint 01 establishes the platform interfaces, native-target build/core-test CI matrix and a recorded support plan without importing Windows-only APIs into the shared core. Record actual job results per target and clearly pending later-platform gates; do not infer runtime support from compilation.
evidence: ../reports/sprint-01.md#test-evidence. Three native CI jobs configured. Hosted job execution remains open.

scenario: Launch the real native feasibility app on Windows and drive text input/copy, focus, pane/context resizing and quit through native controls. Record renderer/process evidence and early macOS/Linux smoke attempts separately. No browser engine or in-process UI snapshot is presented as native-process E2E proof. Each later released OS repeats this proof on its own target.
evidence: ../reports/sprint-01.md#test-evidence and ../reports/evidence/windows-e2e/native.json. Earlier Linux and macOS results recorded separately.

scenario: Exercise the actual supported platform's protected credential store and per-user data path, including unavailable/locked store, Unicode paths, restart and same-user PAT renewal. No plaintext fallback or new duplicate profile appears; offline cached reading and original outbox identity survive. Windows closes initially in Sprint 03; later OS adapters repeat it in their phases.

The packaged target app delivers a native notification, opens the exact item through cold/warm single-instance activation, honors notification preferences, and exposes unsupported actions/replacement semantics honestly with in-app alternatives. Close/Quit, optional background residence, wake and startup behavior preserve pause/offline settings and user data. Windows closes initially in Sprint 11, with clean-machine packaging repeated at release; later OS phases require their own integration evidence.

The macOS milestone passes applicable product/credential/lifecycle/notification/native E2E/performance/installation gates for its published support matrix. It preserves the Windows feature contract and no-browser constraint. Windows completion is not reused as macOS evidence, and Windows regressions from shared changes are checked.

The Linux milestone passes applicable product/credential/lifecycle/notification/native E2E/performance/installation gates for every claimed distribution/desktop/session/architecture combination. Missing graphics, secure-store or system prerequisites produce truthful guidance; untested variants are not declared supported. Previously released platform regressions are checked.

Implement and run the unit-test command on the Sprint 01 core and subsequently introduced domain behavior, with deterministic fixtures, meaningful exit status and machine-readable results. The initial gate proves the runner and current tests, not future feature coverage; every sprint extends its own relevant units.

Use actual SQLite storage and the real HTTP provider adapter against a deterministic local server to verify transactional identity/cache behavior, pagination, partial failures and authentication/error mapping. Storage foundations are tested in Sprint 02 and the initial complete adapter scenario closes in Sprint 03. Later integration scenarios extend this foundation rather than being claimed complete early.

Run the full native application E2E journey for the completed phase: cached startup, search, PR body/issue context switching, preserved inline draft, offline submission, Outbox inspection/cancellation, reconnect/reconciliation, changed-head guards, notification activation and restart. Evidence identifies the actual app process, controls, local database and provider requests; unit calls or GPUI snapshots cannot satisfy it.

Deterministically inject response loss after server success, a crash around dispatch, disk/transaction failure, cancel-versus-reconnect races and revision changes. Native/integration evidence shows retained input, stable target/operation identities, safe dependency holds and no blind duplicate send, false cancellation or lost local data. Run applicable cases throughout the feature sprints and the complete matrix at phase release.

The phase report links every applicable requirement/AC/scenario to unit, integration, native E2E, installer and approved live evidence or an explicit failure/block. Commands, versions, OS/architecture and artifacts are recorded; later-platform statuses stay separate. A skipped or unavailable required native test prevents that platform's publication, not an unsupported all-platform pass.

On a clean supported target with declared system prerequisites and no Rust/compiler checkout, follow the real published install instructions in one to three commands. The per-user app installs and launches; normal OS trust prompts are explained. A placeholder URL or source-build command fails this release gate.

A wrong OS/architecture/version, incompatible prerequisite, truncated artifact, altered checksum/signature or unauthenticated payload is rejected before replacing the installed app. The previous install and user data remain usable, and the explanation plus safe retry path is actionable.

Seed cached content, drafts, a non-default workspace, credentials, pause/offline flags, checkpoints and unresolved Outbox work, then rerun the installer and upgrade from the previous supported version. State and operation identity survive, registrations are not duplicated, and networking respects restored controls. Test interruptions, running-app locks and safe migration recovery without replaying a restored stale Outbox snapshot.

Exercise denied permission, blocked/interrupted download, full disk, failed trust verification and missing prerequisite. Report a concise reason/nonzero exit and safe repair/rerun guidance without requiring developer compilation, an app PAT, security weakening, or silent system changes.

Uninstall removes the application and registrations while retaining local data by default. Explicit data/credential removal is separate and explains pending-work impact. Reinstall restores the retained local profile and incremental progress without an implicit full archive or duplicate queued actions.

The released platform's binaries, version/architecture manifest, authenticity metadata, tested install/update/uninstall commands and clean-machine evidence are actually published. Documentation contains no unresolved placeholder presented as runnable; unreleased platform examples remain clearly labeled templates and do not imply that their packages exist.
